title: Playback: Hi, Hi, Hi by Wings | 1972
content:
Studio One, Morgan Studios, London
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: Mike Bobak

Wings held a playback of their live recordings on 1 September 1972.

They had borrowed the Rolling Stones Mobile Studio to record their shows in Groningen, Amsterdam, The Hague, Antwerp, and Berlin during the Wings Over Europe Tour in August. Paul McCartney was considering releasing a live single, with ‘Hi, Hi, Hi’ the most likely contender, and the Groningen performance was chosen as the best.

Wings’ drummer Denny Seiwell was still in New York, but the rest of the group gathered at Morgan Studios to listen to the recordings and note aspects that would require re-recording.

During the playback session McCartney began improvising a reggae-style song at the piano. The rest of the band joined in, resulting in ‘C Moon’.

I was looking for a reggaeish kind of song. ‘L’ and ‘7’ put together mean ‘square’ in American jive talk: the ‘L’ had been one part of the square and the ‘7’ had formed the other part. I thought, what’s ‘cool’ then? So we had a ‘C’ and a half moon for the other half and we figured that ‘C Moon’ meant cool.
Paul McCartney
Club Sandwich 47/48, Spring 1988
Page last updated: 21 November 2025
